pos.personaBrief: Spain 2008 was built on Xavi and Iniesta with possession and 'dueño del balón, dueño del juego', but also counter-attacked in the final; he sees the ball as control, not as a mere tool for chances.

pro.personaBrief: Aragonés installed short-passing 'toque' with small midfielders, patient and controlled, while still using counters (Torres winner); no verified build-up source, so he leans to patience.

est.personaBrief: Traditional 4-4-2 or 4-1-4-1 with clear roles, but Xavi, Iniesta, Silva and Villa assisting Torres combined in close spaces.

lar.personaBrief: El Debate notes he lacked vertical wingers and relied on central goalscorers Torres and Villa and small central midfielders; five-man midfield with Silva inside.

blo.personaBrief: Atlético 1976/77 was the least scored-against side, but Spain 2008 controlled play and did not sit deep; Germany pressed in the final, evidence on his pressing is thin.

mar.personaBrief: No source on marking; an old-school Spanish coach of the 70s-80s with a pragmatic mindset, likely favouring individual responsibility and close marking of stars, zonal in corners unknown.

pla.personaBrief: He imposed the toque de balón on Spain from the start and stuck to his guns against press criticism; squad unchanged and the plan kept.

res.personaBrief: A pragmatic winner who said if Euro was not won it was his fault; the final showed control and counters, he cares about trophies.

sis.personaBrief: Built a collective around Xavi, Iniesta, Villa, Torres where individuals serve the group (RFEF), with duties for all.

jog.personaBrief: He said Spain lacked physical condition but had players to be superior with the ball; chose small technical midfielders over big ones.

bas.personaBrief: He dropped Raúl and built around young Xavi, Iniesta, Villa, Torres, Fabregas; but trusts proven players more than academy ideology.

lid.personaBrief: Strong-willed 'stubborn mule' who held out against Marca and dropped Raúl, with strong authority and motivation of youngsters like Torres.
